inspection_outcome: Initial scientific review complete within the exact author-manuscript scope; one Major and three Minor findings with explicit evidence and repair limits.
summary: The full Aut^0_N range may lack the necessary ribbon structure. The paper's H_2 admits a cointegral-fixing Hopf involution exchanging both roots of the distinguished grouplike. Local cup, crossing tensor and normalization formulas also need correction. The conditional Seifert/filtration argument and key ADO algebra receive positive checks.

problems.title: The full cointegral-fixing automorphism group need not admit the required ribbon structure
problems.source_location: PDF/printed p.3, 'defined for any rho' and Theorem 1; p.13, Section 3.4, inference to G'-ribbon for G=Aut^0_{N^m}(H); p.20, Section 4. Correct restricted assumptions occur on pp.8-9; counterexample algebra is defined on pp.24-25.
problems.claim: Degree preservation and fixing the left cointegral, together with D(H) ribbon, suffice for the stated full automorphism range of the twisted invariant.
problems.assumptions: Ordinary Hopf algebra over C; H=H_2 from Section 5, dimension 16, k^8=1, E^2=0, kE=iEk, Delta(E)=E tensor k^2+1 tensor E, deg E=1, deg k=0. D(H_2) is ribbon with the paper's valid KR pair.
problems.check_method: Root independently reconstructed the Hopf involution, cointegral and right integral, proved the complete grouplike list by grading, and compared the identity-fibre ribbon invariance condition. Exact Gaussian-integer basis arithmetic corroborates the example. Read and actually viewed the corresponding propositions in both exact versions of reference [23].
problems.decisive_evidence: tau(k)=k^5,tau(E)=E preserves multiplication/coproduct/grading, tau^2=id, and fixes Lambda=(sum_{j=0}^7 k^j)E. The right integral lambda(k^6 E)=1 yields distinguished a=k^6. All grouplikes are k^j, so b^2=a only permits b=k^3,k^7; tau swaps them. Every ribbon structure requires a G-invariant such b (reference [23] v2, Proposition 2.3, p.9). Hence no <tau>-ribbon structure exists, although tau is in Aut^0_N(H_2). A knot meridian may map to tau through abelianization; tau theta still swaps these roots.
problems.result: Confirmed obstruction to the asserted construction and advertised representation range, including a failure of the p.13 inference. Not a numerical counterexample to an already defined genus invariant.
problems.counterevidence: Section 2.4 explicitly requires fixing b,beta, and Section 3 opens with a G-ribbon hypothesis. Reading that standing condition as an additional restriction saves the conditional argument, but does not justify the advertised full Aut^0 range. The exterior-algebra example and ADO degree-scaling subgroup preserve their ribbon data. Reference [23] v1 already has the fixed-pair condition; v2 classifies it.
problems.impact: Theorem 1's applicability and the existence of the invariant for all stated rho must be restricted; no claim that the whole paper or its conditional degree bound is false.

correction.statement: Take an explicitly specified G subset Aut^0_{N^m}(H) fixing a chosen valid KR pair (b,beta), with the required square-root character, and require im rho subset G; alternatively explicitly assume the corresponding G-ribbon structure and its graded extension.
correction.verification: For the fixed-pair repair, grouplikes have degree zero and characters kill the positive-degree nilpotent ideal, so theta fixes b,beta. The square-root character and the filtration argument then apply. The corrected universal classification is consistent with reference [23] v2 Proposition 2.3.
correction.status: Concrete restricted-scope repair checked; no author adoption asserted

source_locations: Reference [23] v1 and v2 pp.8-9; v2 Proposition 2.3
independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: For H over C generated by k,E with k^8=1,E^2=0,kE=iEk and coproduct E tensor k^2+1 tensor E, the basis k^j E^a has dimension16, degree E=1. tau(k)=k^5,tau(E)=E is a degree-preserving involutive Hopf automorphism: i^5=i,k^10=k^2,25=1 mod8. It fixes Lambda=sum k^jE, so r_H(tau)=1. The right integral lambda(k^6E)=1 gives distinguished grouplike a=k^6. All grouplikes have degree0, and b^2=a permits only k^3,k^7, interchanged by tau. D(H) is nevertheless ribbon: b=k^3,beta(k)=exp(3pi i/4),beta(E)=0 satisfy beta^2=the distinguished character and the Kauffman--Radford S^2 condition. Reference [23]'s classification requires G-invariance of both grouplikes; none of the possible b is tau-invariant. Naturality of the canonical Drinfeld element also forces an invariant pivot if the neutral ribbon is invariant. Normalization beta(1)=1 precludes compensating scalar factors.
independent_acceptance_check.assumption_test: Finite-dimensional nonnegative grading, r_H(tau)=1 and ordinary ribbon-double conditions all hold. A knot abelianization Z to C2 with meridian tau lies in the stated representation range. Adding the degree twist does not fix the swapped b because it fixes k.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence: Earlier source pp.8-9 explicitly assume a fixed pair and a square-root homomorphism, but p.13 replaces the group by the full graded r_H=1 subgroup. The degree-scaling ADO and exterior-algebra applications preserve their selected pair. No numerical genus inequality counterexample is claimed.
independent_acceptance_check.dependency_and_severity: The missing equivariant ribbon structure obstructs definition of the claimed invariant for the advertised full group, hence a core Major construction defect, despite a natural subgroup repair.
independent_acceptance_check.repair: Restrict to the subgroup preserving an admissible pair and require the square-root character; restrict rho accordingly. Homogeneous degree scaling preserves grouplikes and characters and does not introduce this obstruction.

problems.title: The right cup coefficient fails the snake identity
problems.source_location: PDF/printed p.29, Section 5.6, first displayed cap/cup formulas; compare the pivot on p.25 and module action on p.28.
problems.claim: The displayed right caps and cups implement the pivotal evaluation/coevaluation and can be pasted to define the ADO tangle invariant.
problems.assumptions: p>=2; zeta_p=exp(pi i/p); basis v_i and its ordinary dual; generic alpha may be used.
problems.check_method: Root read the actual page image, multiplied the diagonal cap/cup coefficients, and independently recovered the cap from the pivot g_alpha=zeta_p^{-alpha(p-1)} bar{k}^{2p+2}.
problems.decisive_evidence: The printed coefficients a_i=zeta_p^{alpha(1-p)-2i}, b_i=zeta_p^{-alpha(1-p)-2i} give a_i b_i=zeta_p^{-4i}. At p=3,i=1 the snake is multiplication by zeta_3^2, not 1. This is independent of alpha.
problems.result: Confirmed failure of the local duality identity for the displayed cup.
problems.counterevidence: The cap coefficient agrees with the actual pivot, and the proof states that the two maps should use g_alpha^{+/-1}. At p=2 the defect is masked because every zeta_2^{-4i}=1. The corrected pivotal formalism remains available.
problems.impact: Literal reproduction from the displayed cup fails tangle duality. The problem is a local exponent sign and does not establish failure of the corrected ADO invariant or its genus bound.

correction.statement: Replace the cup coefficient by zeta_p^{-alpha(1-p)+2i}=a_i^{-1}.
correction.verification: The corrected snake product is identically 1 on every v_i, for all alpha and p>=2. This matches g_alpha^{-1}.

source_locations: Primary p.29 right caps and cups; preceding pivot definition
independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: With q=exp(pi i/p), the printed coefficients a_i=q^{alpha(1-p)-2i} and b_i=q^{-alpha(1-p)-2i} give a_i b_i=q^{-4i}. For p=3,i=1 this is q^2, not1, independently of generic alpha. Changing the cup exponent from -2i to +2i makes it the inverse of the pivot eigenvalue and restores both snake contractions.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence: p=2 masks the error. The conceptual prescription uses g_alpha and g_alpha^{-1} correctly; the defect is the displayed coordinate formula, not a proof that the ADO invariant fails.
independent_acceptance_check.repair: Correct the cup index sign and retain the inverse-pivot prescription.

problems.title: The formal tensor R_D omits the sign of negative crossings
problems.source_location: PDF/printed p.12, displayed definition of R_D; compare the explicit negative-crossing rule on p.11.
problems.claim: The displayed tensor product of R_{alpha_j,beta_j}, without sign exponents, implements the preceding rule for diagrams with either crossing sign.
problems.assumptions: Already exposed by ordinary H=C[C3], trivial G, degree zero; no super sign or nonabelian labels are needed.
problems.check_method: Root compared actual p.11/p.12 images and independently used the double of C[C3].
problems.decisive_evidence: For generator g of C3 and delta_j dual to g^j, R=sum_j (epsilon tensor g^j) tensor (delta_j tensor 1), whereas R^{-1}=sum_j (epsilon tensor g^{-j}) tensor (delta_j tensor 1). They differ at j=1. For a single negative open crossing the following permutation is invertible and both strand multiplications are identities, so the tensor difference survives.
problems.result: Confirmed mismatch between the formal tensor and the correct negative bead rule.
problems.counterevidence: Page 11 correctly uses R^{-1}; later informal bead computations can and do use that rule. This is not a demonstrated failure of the invariant defined by the correct rules.
problems.impact: The formal total formula needs the crossing sign for literal computation; a local correction is sufficient for this mismatch.

correction.statement: Use the tensor product of R_{alpha_j,beta_j}^{sign(c_j)}, retaining p.11's edge-label and crossing-map conventions.
correction.verification: For the C3 example the inverse tensor multiplies R to the unit. Single-crossing distinction is exact.

source_locations: Primary pp.11-12 universal crossing tensor formula
independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: The aggregate tensor formula omits the inverse at a negative crossing although the preceding local rule is sign-sensitive. Already for H=C[C3], trivial automorphism group and degree0, the double's R=sum_j(epsilon tensor g^j) tensor(delta_j tensor1) differs from R^{-1}, which uses g^{-j}; j=1 distinguishes them. A single open crossing followed by the invertible label permutations cannot remove this difference.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence: The local crossing instructions on p.11 are correct and control the intended construction. This is a local formula defect, not a failure of the corrected invariant.
independent_acceptance_check.repair: Insert the crossing-sign power/inverse while preserving the displayed colored tensor labels and order.

problems.title: Two comparison formulas in Proposition 5.4 omit the chosen variable/phase normalization
problems.source_location: PDF/printed pp.29-30, Proposition 5.4 proof: the ADO_p(K,zeta_p^alpha) line and the final epsilon(Z_theta)v0=Z_alpha v0 assertion.
problems.claim: The displayed comparison equations consistently implement t=zeta_p^{2alpha} and the writhe normalization.
problems.assumptions: Use the section's declared t=zeta_p^{2alpha}, writhe w(D), and the correctly normalized pivotal maps.
problems.check_method: Root tracked the k^{2alpha w(D)} factor, the action on v0, and the three scalar exponents.
problems.decisive_evidence: The preceding p.29 formula gives Z_alpha v0=zeta_p^{w alpha^2} sum_{i,j} lambda_{ij0} zeta_p^{alpha(i-j)/2}v0. Thus epsilon(Z_theta)|_{t=zeta_p^{2alpha}} v0=zeta_p^{-w alpha^2}Z_alpha v0, not Z_alpha v0. The proof's ADO argument should be zeta_p^{2alpha}, consistent with the immediately preceding definition.
problems.result: Confirmed two local normalization inconsistencies; corrected exponents lead to the asserted final equality.
problems.counterevidence: At w=0 the missing writhe factor disappears. Restoring it cancels the -w alpha^2 term in the ADO normalization and leaves zeta_p^{w alpha(p-1)}=t^{w(p-1)/2}. Hence this is not evidence against the final intended equality.
problems.impact: The written proof is inconsistent away from zero writhe; the intended variable and scalar correction repair this algebraic step.

correction.statement: Use ADO_p(K,zeta_p^{2alpha}) and insert zeta_p^{-w alpha^2} in the last comparison.
correction.verification: w(-alpha^2+alpha(p-1))+w alpha^2=w alpha(p-1), exactly the normalization in equation (2).
correction.status: Algebraic repair verified; full independent knot-table reproduction not claimed

independent_acceptance_check.independent_derivation: The declared variable is t=q^{2alpha}, whereas one proof line writes ADO_p(K,q^alpha). On v_0, Z_alpha has scalar q^{w alpha^2} sum lambda_ij0 q^{alpha(i-j)/2}; therefore epsilon(Z^theta)=q^{-w alpha^2} times that scalar. The printed equality omits the phase. For p=3,alpha=1/2,w=1 the phase is exp(pi i/12), nontrivial. Restoring it yields q^{w(-alpha^2+alpha(p-1))}q^{w alpha^2}=q^{w alpha(p-1)}=t^{w(p-1)/2}, the required normalization.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence: Zero writhe hides the phase, and the corrected normalization proves the intended comparison; no counterexample to Proposition5.4's corrected identity is asserted.
independent_acceptance_check.repair: Use t=q^{2alpha} consistently and include the writhe phase in the counit/eigenvalue equality.

clarifications.point: The zero-polynomial degree needs a convention; genus zero is handled by the straight unknot. These are boundary clarifications, not a constructed numerical counterexample.

Coefficient cancellation may remove candidate extrema. The displayed nonexhaustive negative-power filtration nevertheless contains every proof term after the explicit pivot shift. Neither observation refutes the width bound.
The square-root character is defined on additive C; it need not descend to the automorphism image. No error is inferred from non-descent at even p.
The dual antipode uses p composed with S^{-1}; a candidate based on p composed with S was withdrawn.
The ribbon proposition is numbered2.3 in both acquired versions, not2.4; its fixed-pair hypothesis is the substantive dependency.

limitations: Assessment applies to arXiv2211.15010v1 (28Nov2022), not automatically to publisher version accepted12Oct2023/published24Feb2025.
No numerical genus-bound counterexample was found or asserted. Conditional argument survives the admissible ribbon restriction.
Local sign/scalar repairs are verified; full all-knot reproduction and all categorical invariance moves were not repeated.
Related 2025 talk code/handout are not established as formal journal supplement or complete reproduction package; missing original code is not a defect.
